original_question: Which disease is typically recognized shortly after birth, cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita or glaucoma?

final_qi.question: Is cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita typically recognized shortly after birth?
final_qi.long_answer: Cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita (CMTC) is a congenital vascular anomaly characterized by a persistent, marbled (reticular) vascular pattern of the skin. In the vast majority of reported cases, the distinctive skin findings are already present at birth or become evident within the first days to weeks of life. Because the mottled, violaceous reticulated pattern is usually obvious on initial newborn examination, CMTC is typically recognized shortly after birth rather than later in childhood. This timing of recognition is well-documented in clinical descriptions and reviews of the disorder, supporting that early postnatal identification is the norm.

final_qi.question: Is glaucoma typically recognized shortly after birth?
final_qi.long_answer: Most forms of glaucoma, especially primary open-angle glaucoma (the commonest type), develop slowly and are usually diagnosed in mid- to late adulthood, often after age 40. Although a rare congenital form of glaucoma can be detected in the neonatal period or early infancy, this represents a very small minority of cases. Therefore, glaucoma is not typically recognized shortly after birth according to established ophthalmologic consensus.
